chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman and enters into her (consummates the marriage) before giving her anything. He said: It is a debt upon him.

key_terms.أبو عبد الله: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.دخول: Entering into the wife, referring to consummation of marriage
key_terms.مهر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband's obligation to pay the dowry if he consummates the marriage before making any payment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that consummating marriage before paying any portion of the stipulated dowry (mahr) does not invalidate the union but converts the unpaid amount into a binding debt (dayn) upon the husband. This ruling underscores the financial security of the wife in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the delay in payment does not negate her right to the full agreed-upon dowry, a principle consistent with the broader Quranic emphasis on fulfilling financial obligations in marital contracts.
